title: Undecidability of the halting language
statement: Let the halting set consist of codes of programs paired with inputs for which the encoded program halts on the encoded input. Define the halting digit to be $1$ for numbers in this set and $0$ otherwise, and define the halting prefix by $h(0)=0$ and $h(J+1)=4h(J)+	ext{halting digit}(J)$. For a binary string $x$, let $N(x)$ be the length of the output of the specified head transducer on $x$, and let $J(x)$ be the base-$4$ logarithm, rounded down, of the length of the output of the specified rest transducer on $x$. The language consists of strings $x$ satisfying $1\\le J(x)$, $N(x)=h(J(x)-1)$, and membership of $J(x)-1$ in the halting set; this language is not computable.
caveat: The formal statement depends on particular head and rest transducers whose defining behavior is not given in the provided informal descriptions.
